messages.subject: Interpreting `group.w.free = T` with multiple outcomes
parts:
Hello, 

From what I have found, I can set a Poisson distribution to the outcome if I set `group.w.free = T`. According to documentation:

"If TRUE, the group frequencies are considered to be free parameters in the model. In this case, a Poisson model is fitted to estimate the group frequencies."

In this case, does this make only the final outcome interpreted like a poisson regression? I ask because there is no way to set a variable name like you would for an ordinal variable, for example. 

Here's a simplified example which shows what I'm saying

simplified_model <-
'
continuous_outcome ~ predictor 

count_based_outcome ~ continuous_outcome
'

Poisson_fit<- lavaan(simplified_model, data = dat, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml", meanstructure = T, group.w.free = T)

If I run this, is lavaan assuming both `continuous_outcome` and `count_based_outcome` are both count variables, or can I specify this in some way? 

Thanks,
Chris

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Interpreting `group.w.free = T` with multiple outcomes
parts:
On 7/21/20 7:09 PM, christoph...@gmail.com wrote:
> From what I have found, I can set a Poisson distribution to the outcome
> if I set `group.w.free = T`. According to documentation:
>
> /"If TRUE, the group frequencies are considered to be free parameters in
> the model. In this case, a Poisson model is fitted to estimate the group

> frequencies."/

No. You misunderstood. The Poisson model is only used for the group
frequencies themselves. Not the other outcomes of the model.

Yves.
